Run to run consistency, broken down by slice and severity

Source: R/compare.R
consistency_strata.Rd

The flat disagreement rate from [consistency()] answers whether a system is unstable. It does not answer where, and a single number averages a slice that flickers on every call into one that never does. This reports the same instability stratified by slice and by severity, so an unstable slice, or instability concentrated in the critical cases, is visible rather than diluted.

Usage

consistency_strata(run)

Arguments

run

An `r4agent_run` with `repeats` greater than one.

Value

A list with the overall disagreement rate and unstable ids (as [consistency()] returns), plus `by_slice` and `by_severity` data frames giving the case count, unstable count and disagreement rate in each stratum.

Details

A case counts as unstable when it did not return the same verdict on every repeat, exactly as in [consistency()]; the overall figures here are identical to that function's. Only the breakdown is added.

See also

[consistency()]

Examples

suite <- agent_suite(list(
  agent_case("steady", "ping", "ok", slice = "stable", grader = "contains"),
  agent_case("flaky", "toggle", "ok", slice = "shaky", severity = "high",
             grader = "contains")
))
# A deterministic offline runner that flips its answer for one input.
seen <- new.env()
flip <- function(x) {
  n <- if (exists(x, seen, inherits = FALSE)) get(x, seen) else 0L
  assign(x, n + 1L, seen)
  if (x == "toggle" && (n + 1L) %% 2L == 0L) "no" else "ok"
}
run <- run_benchmark(suite, flip, repeats = 4L, quiet = TRUE)
consistency_strata(run)$by_severity
#>   severity n_cases unstable disagreement
#> 1   medium       1        0            0
#> 2     high       1        1            1
